messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Bengali, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Bengali line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
যখন আমি নিচু স্থানে ফিরে যাচ্ছিলাম, আমার চোখের সামনে এক ব্যক্তি উপস্থিত হল যিনি দীর্ঘ নীরবতার পর কণ্ঠস্বর হ্রস্ব শোনাতেন।

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|------------------------|--------| | Mentre | temporal conjunction “while” | যখন | while/when | OK | | ch'i' | contracted “che + io” → “that I” | আমি | I (subject) | OK | | rovinava | imperfect “was falling / going down” | ফিরে যাচ্ছিলাম | was going back / falling | OK | | in | preposition “to / in” (direction) | স্থানে | at the place (locative) | OK | | basso | adjective “low” | নিচু | low | OK | | loco | noun “place” | (part of) স্থানে | place | OK | | dinanzi | adverb/preposition “before / in front of” | সামনে | in front of | OK | | a | preposition linking to “eyes” (to) | চোখের | of the eyes (genitive) | OK | | li | definite article “the” (plural) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (article omitted in Bengali) | | occhi | noun “eyes” | চোখ | eyes | OK | | mi | indirect object “to me” | আমার | my (possessor) | OK | | si | reflexive pronoun used in passive | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (passive sense expressed by verb) | | fu | auxiliary “was” (past remote) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (auxiliary omitted) | | offerto | past participle “presented / offered” | উপস্থিত | presented / appeared | OK | | chi | relative pronoun “who / one who” | যিনি | who (relative) | OK | | per | preposition “through / because of” | নীরবতার | of silence (genitive) | OK | | lungo | adjective “long” | দীর্ঘ | long | OK | | silenzio | noun “silence” | নীরবতা | silence | OK | | parea | verb “seemed” (imperfect) | শোনাতেন | seemed (to be heard) | OK | | fioco | adjective “hoarse / weak” | হ্রস্ব | hoarse / weak | OK |

### Items Flagged
- **UNNECESSARY**: `li`, `si`, `fu` – articles and auxiliary/reflexive particles that have no direct counterpart in Bengali and are naturally omitted.
No source words are **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR**‑incorrect in the Bengali rendering.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Bengali script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Bengali text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
